exposure: having a doula during the labor process
outcome: performance of machine learning in predicting emergency cesarean section
cohort: The study included nulliparous women with a single cephalic pregnancy, >=37 weeks of gestation, and induced or spontaneous labor, who gave birth between January 2020 and December 2022 at a maternal tertiary center in Iran, excluding those with maternal request for C-section or C-section before labor onset.
finding: The linear regression model achieved the best diagnostic performance (AUROC: 0.86) among seven machine learning algorithms in predicting emergency cesarean sections in nulliparous women, identifying several key predictors.
mod_finding: Advanced maternal age and education, diabetes, preeclampsia, placenta abruption, hypothyroidism, meconium amniotic fluid, late-term pregnancy, lack of doula support, and not attending prenatal courses were identified as predictors of emergency cesarean section.
birth_weight: Measured as an exposure; fetal macrosomia linked to cesarean section.
gest_age: >=37 weeks of gestation; also an exposure factor (late-term pregnancy was a predictor).
